venues.n: Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club
venues.d: A restored 1930s beach club turned Richard Meier landmark — the most complete luxury address on the Miami sand.
A serene Art Deco-meets-Asian sanctuary on Collins Avenue — the quietest true luxury on the beach.
Alan Faena's theatrical red-and-gold fantasy — a Damien Hirst gilded mammoth and a cabaret theatre on the sand.

venues.n: Acqualina Resort & Residences on the Beach
venues.d: A Mediterranean palazzo on the Sunny Isles sand — Forbes Five-Star for hotel and spa, fourteen years running.

venues.n: The St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort
venues.d: The grand oceanfront St. Regis beside Bal Harbour Shops — butler service and a rarefied, moneyed calm.
A living-green, reclaimed-wood sanctuary on Collins — sustainable luxury with four pools and the beach at the door.
The Nobu world made a hotel inside the Eden Roc — Japanese-minimalist rooms above the flagship restaurant.
The Cipriani family's intimate Italian-styled tower over the Grove — old-world Venetian service in leafy Miami.
A colonial-white Ocean Drive landmark with a literary soul — the most cultured small hotel in South Beach.
Ian Schrager's polished, playful oceanfront tower — a skating rink and bowling alley beneath quiet-luxury rooms.
The Robuchon counter in the Design District — the only two-star table in Florida, for a third year running.
Thomas Keller's continental grand room inside the Four Seasons Surf Club — old-glamour Miami at its most refined.
The Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse from New York — smokeless grills, dry-aged beef and endless Champagne.
Michael Beltran's New-American-meets-Cuban cooking in the Grove — personal, Miami-rooted and quietly excellent.
A tiny, cult Italian-American counter in a strip mall — outsized cooking, no ceremony, a real find.
Alain Verzeroli's garden-driven French room in the Design District — seasonal, light and beautifully composed.
Juan Manuel Barrientos's multisensory Colombian tasting menu — theatre, memory and Andean flavour in Brickell.
Masa-driven modern Mexican in the Grove — a Green Star kitchen built on heirloom corn and local produce.
Top Chef winner Jeremy Ford's refined, ingredient-led room — a Green Star for its sustainable kitchen.
A twelve-seat counter from Evan Burgess and Osmel Gonzalez — hyper-local, sustainable, deeply personal.
Shingo Akikuni's fourteen-seat omakase in the Gables — pristine edomae sushi of great precision.
An eight-seat omakase behind a hidden door in Wynwood — Seijun Okano's singular, secret counter.
Refined Edomae-style omakase paired with rare Japanese whiskies — quiet mastery north of the city centre.
Tristan Brandt's French cooking with Asian notes inside the Carillon — a jewel-box tasting-menu room.
The world's first kosher restaurant to earn a Michelin star — Raz Shabtai's inventive seasonal Middle Eastern.
Chef Niven Patel's farm-driven Indian cooking — coastal curries and roasted vegetables from his own fields.
The definitive Cuban sandwich, made from scratch — house-cured meats and pressed medianoche on Calle Ocho.
Vietnamese-Cajun cooking with real swagger — a beloved, boldly flavoured MiMo institution.
The Brooklyn pizza legend's Miami outpost — thin-crust pies made one at a time, worth the wait.

venues.n: Ocean Drive & the Art Deco Historic District
venues.d: A mile of pastel 1920s–30s hotels in candy colours, neon and porthole windows — the largest concentration of Art Deco architecture in the world. Walk it early morning before the heat, camera in hand; the multi-gen crowd loves it and the light on the facades is best just after sunrise.

venues.n: Art Deco walking tour (Miami Design Preservation League)
venues.d: The definitive 90-minute guided walk from the 1001 Ocean Drive welcome centre, decoding the streamline-moderne facades, the theming, and how a preservation battle in the 1980s saved the district. A cultured, easy outing for parents and grandparents who want the story, not just the photo.

The world's largest outdoor street-art museum — a curated open-air courtyard of monumental murals by 120-plus artists from 25-plus countries, rotated regularly. Entry is now timed and ticketed through the welcome centre, so pre-book; the surrounding streets are free to roam.

venues.n: Wynwood Arts District galleries & mural streets
venues.d: Beyond the Walls, the whole neighbourhood is a canvas — galleries, warehouses, breweries and cafes wrapped in ever-changing murals. Come on a Second Saturday Art Walk when studios open late; a relaxed evening for design-minded families before dinner.

A walkable open-air quarter where flagship maisons — Louis Vuitton, Dior, Hermès, Cartier, Bulgari — sit among public art, Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome and sculpture-lined plazas. Serious shopping paired with architecture and art, valet-easy and unhurried.

A sharp, free-admission contemporary-art museum with a sculpture garden, set right in the Design District so you can pair it with the boutiques. A quick, refined cultural stop that never feels like homework.

James Deering's 1916 Italian-Renaissance villa on Biscayne Bay, with formal gardens, a stone barge breakwater and antique-filled rooms — the most romantic estate in Miami. A multi-generational favourite; go on a weekday morning and linger in the gardens before the tour crowds.

Herzog & de Meuron's hanging-garden pavilion on the downtown bayfront holds 20th- and 21st-century international art, with terraces over Biscayne Bay. The cafe and shaded verandah make it easy with elders and children in tow.

venues.n: Phillip & Patricia Frost Museum of Science
venues.d: A planetarium, a three-level aquarium and hands-on galleries share the bayfront park with PAMM — the two sell a combo pass. The most reliable half-day for grandchildren, with plenty of air-conditioned space when the sun is fierce.

Miami Beach's contemporary-art museum in a restored 1930s Art Deco building by Russell Pancoast — the first public exhibition space in South Florida. Compact and beautifully curated, a short walk from Collins Avenue and easy to fold into a beach day.

One of the largest private contemporary-art collections in the U.S., shown across a converted warehouse complex with a courtyard, garden and excellent restaurant. A quieter, connoisseur's alternative to the marquee museums — ideal for collectors.

An experiential-art destination built for immersive installations — mirrored infinity rooms and light works you walk through. Genuinely wondrous for children and grown-ups alike; book a timed slot and pair it with the Rubell nearby.

The heart of Cuban Miami — cigar rollers, fruit stands, rum bars, galleries and the aroma of cafecito along SW 8th Street. Come for the walk, the music and a guava pastry; the veg-aware will find plenty in the fruit shakes and rice-and-plantain plates.

A tiny corner park where elders have gathered over dominoes and heated debate for four decades — pure, unstaged neighbourhood life. Open daily; stand at the rail and watch, a memorable few minutes for grandparents who recognise the ritual.

A live-music landmark on Calle Ocho since 1935, with indoor and courtyard stages, salsa and no cover charge. An authentic Havana-style evening — free salsa lessons on Thursdays if the younger set wants to try.

A 1926 Mediterranean-revival landmark with a soaring lobby, a Donald Ross golf course and the largest hotel pool on the U.S. East Coast, set in 150 acres. Take afternoon tea or a heritage tour even if you're not staying — grand, hushed, old-world luxury.
A 1923 swimming grotto carved from a coral-rock quarry, fed by spring water, with caves, waterfalls and Venetian bridges. A one-of-a-kind, storybook swim for the whole family on a hot afternoon.

83 acres of palms, cycads, flowering trees and a butterfly conservatory, with a tram if walking is tiring. Serene and shaded — a gentle morning for elders and a wonder for children, especially during the seasonal art and orchid shows.

A leafy, Mediterranean-styled main street of boutiques, galleries and fine restaurants, with fountains and canopy trees. A civilised, low-key afternoon of strolling and shopping away from the beach crowds.

venues.n: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park & Lighthouse
venues.d: The tip of Key Biscayne, with the 1825 Cape Florida Light — the oldest standing structure in Miami-Dade — and a calm, palm-backed beach 15 minutes from downtown. Climb the 109 steps for views over Stiltsville and the skyline; two Cuban-food cafes on site make an easy family day.

A two-mile crescent of soft sand with shallow, gentle water and cabanas — one of the calmest, most family-friendly beaches near the city. Quieter than South Beach; good for grandparents and small children who want the sea without the scene.

The iconic wide white-sand beach backed by pastel lifeguard stands and the Art Deco skyline. Rent a private cabana for shade and service; the promenade behind is perfect for an evening stroll with the family.

A refined, low-rise stretch of sand fronting the luxury enclave, linked by a shaded oceanfront boardwalk toward Surfside. Calm and discreet — the beach of choice if you want quiet luxury over spectacle.
A broad, uncrowded beach lined with gleaming towers — favoured by international families for space and its easy villa-and-condo stays. Wide sand, warm water and a relaxed pace for a multi-day base.

The most exclusive open-air mall in America — Chanel, Dior, Prada, Cartier and an expanded Tiffany among koi ponds and tropical greenery, anchored by Neiman Marcus and Saks. A major 2026 expansion is nearly doubling its size; peerless, unhurried luxury shopping with valet and fine dining.

The largest mall in South Florida — 300-plus stores balancing Hermès, Gucci and Louis Vuitton with everyday favourites and Nordstrom and Bloomingdale's anchors. Fully covered and cool, with a play area and slide tower for children; the practical choice for big family shopping.

A 90-minute sightseeing cruise from Bayside past the waterfront mansions of Star, Palm and Hibiscus Islands and the downtown skyline. Charter a private yacht instead for a bespoke sunset run — the classic way to see Miami's wealth from the water.

A waterfront marketplace of shops, cafes and live music beside the marina where most bay cruises depart, next to the green sweep of Bayfront Park. An easy, walkable staging point before a boat tour, with the skyline as backdrop.
Miami's oldest neighbourhood — leafy, bohemian and bayfront, with sidewalk cafes, sailing marinas and the CocoWalk arcade. A gentle, tree-shaded afternoon; pair it with Vizcaya just up the road.

Miami's glossy financial district, with a climate-controlled open-air shopping and dining complex, rooftop bars and river-mouth views. Sleek and cosmopolitan — good for an evening of dining and skyline drinks.

A Caribbean-styled arts centre with a gallery, dance and a marketplace, hosting Konpa concerts and guided neighbourhood tours through the culture and food of Haitian Miami. An off-the-beaten-path cultural afternoon most visitors miss.

The northern gateway to the Everglades, where a 15-mile paved loop — by tram, bike or foot — puts alligators and wading birds within arm's reach, ending at a lookout tower over the sawgrass. A genuine wilderness half-day, naturalist-guided and gentle enough for all ages.

A fast, exhilarating glide across the wetlands with a wildlife show and gators up close, at parks along the Tamiami Trail west of the city. Book a private boat for a calmer, unhurried run; a thrill the grandchildren will talk about for years.

venues.n: Key West & the Florida Keys day-trip
venues.d: A scenic drive down the Overseas Highway across turquoise water to Florida's southernmost city — Duval Street, Hemingway's house, Mallory Square sunsets and reef snorkelling. Long but rewarding; consider a chauffeur or a stay overnight to do it at leisure.

The gentler, closer Keys escape — sport-fishing capital, sandbar picnics, tarpon feeding and waterfront seafood, an hour and a half south. A relaxed alternative to the full Key West haul, easy as a private half-day charter.

A pedestrian promenade of shops, cafes and galleries designed by Morris Lapidus, lined with fountains and shaded seating a block from the beach. An easy, car-free evening stroll for browsing and people-watching.

A theatrical enclave of Alan Faena's making — a gilded Damien Hirst mammoth, a Rem Koolhaas-designed cultural forum and a hotel dripping in Baz Luhrmann drama. Come for a drink and the spectacle even if you stay elsewhere; unabashed, cinematic luxury.

Kenneth Treister's powerful sculptural memorial — a giant bronze hand rising amid figures, set in a contemplative garden. A quiet, moving stop of real gravity a short walk from the Convention Center and Botanical Garden.
A serene 2.6-acre green pocket of palms, orchids, a Japanese garden and lily ponds in the middle of the city — and free to enter. A cool, shaded pause between the beach and the Convention Center.

A design-and-decorative-arts museum in a striking 1927 building, exploring how design shaped the modern age — propaganda, industry, Art Deco objects. A thoughtful, air-conditioned hour for design-minded visitors on Washington Avenue.

A vast cage-free, walk-and-tram safari park with Asian and African habitats and a Florida section — one of the country's largest zoos. A full, gentle family day; go early to beat the heat, and use the tram to spare tired legs.

Charles Deering's bayfront estate — historic houses, a fossil-rich hammock, mangrove shoreline and canoe access, quieter than its famous sibling Vizcaya. A tranquil nature-and-history morning for those who like their culture uncrowded.

A man-made tidal atoll pool ringed by sand and palms beside Biscayne Bay, calm and shallow with the skyline in the distance. One of the safest, prettiest swims for small children, with a marina and cafe alongside.
A pretty pedestrian lane of Mediterranean-revival buildings, string lights, tapas terraces and buskers a block off Ocean Drive. A charming spot for an early-evening aperitivo before dinner.

venues.n: Pérez-area sunset sail / private yacht charter
venues.d: Beyond the group cruises, Biscayne Bay is made for a private catamaran or motor-yacht charter — a captain, a chef, veg-friendly catering and a swim stop off a sandbar. The most memorable evening on the water, tailored entirely to your family.

venues.n: Nightlife on Washington Avenue & the rooftops
venues.d: Miami's after-dark reputation is earned — from South Beach clubs to rooftop lounges over Brickell and the Design District's sleeker bars. For UHNI guests, a host or table-service arrangement smooths the night; the concierge can curate a discreet, easy evening.
Julio Cabrera's Havana-style cantina — the finest Cuban cocktails in America, poured by master cantineros.
A refined, ingredient-driven cocktail room that broke into the region's very best — Miami's newest star bar.
The garden bar that put Miami on the world cocktail map — herb-driven, barefoot-glamour drinking by the pool.
John Lermayer's warm, all-day neighbourhood bar — serious cocktails without a shred of pretension.
A drink amid Faena's gilded, red-velvet theatre — the most glamorous hotel bar in Miami Beach.

venues.n: The Bar at The Surf Club
venues.d: A jewel-box bar in a restored 1930s beach club — Winston Churchill drank here; the glamour is real.
A Balinese-styled rooftop garden on the 40th floor — the highest bar in the city, with 360° bay-and-skyline views.
